grf.observed_reality: Exact current main artifact builds and executes on the upstream self-hosted Linux x64 lane and the same bytes execute in an independent Linux sandbox.
grf.retained_hypothesis: The one-file product boundary is viable for the currently admitted canonical Clay subset.
grf.strongest_counter_reality: The apparent one-file portability may still fail on compatible-but-older GNU/Linux or constrained temporary filesystems even when the file itself is intact.
grf.discriminator: Run the exact EntityOS bytes on the declared oldest supported Ubuntu/glibc floor and on a clean target with controlled temporary-directory execution constraints; keep failures separate from Clay semantic failures.

primary_external_evidence.claim: onefile is a single bundled executable but unpacks support files to a temporary directory at runtime; POSIX noexec or unsuitable temp locations can prevent execution
GNU/Linux bundles do not bundle libc; binaries built on newer glibc may fail on older systems, so the oldest intended supported Linux should be used as the build floor

portable execution across the declared Linux compatibility floor
